events.text: Elder Gyeol of the Grey Cloud finds you on a fog-bound jetty and warms both hands on a lantern that gives no heat. "You tie your dead to a drifting rope like a gardener ties vines," the Elder says. "They are owed more than tea. The Court of the Unrisen teaches what grudges are for." The cranes will not land near the lantern.

choices.text: Ask what it costs

effects.log: Elder Gyeol smiles and names nothing. The lantern gutters, which is an answer of a kind.

choices.text: Say you will think about it

effects.log: The Elder inclines a grey head. "Think on a rainy night," is the answer. "Rain is when we are best heard."

events.text: On the rim of a burned-out sky-garden the Elder lets you hold the grey cord while he talks. A grudge, says Elder Gyeol, is only a wish with directions. Name a wonhon of the Isles, hand it the name of a rival immortal, and let the Cloud-Knot carry it. Your fingers tremble on the cord, and the cord does not seem to mind.

choices.text: Practise on the cord until your hands stop shaking

effects.log: Hour after hour on the burned terrace. By dusk the tremor is gone, and you wish it had stayed.

choices.text: Ask what became of the last student

effects.log: The Elder looks at the clouds. "Promoted," he says. You decide not to ask where.

events.text: The second lesson is a knot, tied between two names and pulled tight with a vow. Elder Gyeol of the Grey Cloud calls it the Knot-Oath: what binds a foe binds you. "Mind the weight," he says, setting a grey stone on your palm. The stone is heavier than it ought to be, and warmer.

choices.text: Tie it on the stone until it holds

effects.log: It holds on the ninth try. You feel the oath settle somewhere under the ribs, like a second heartbeat.

choices.text: Ask what happens if the knot is cut

effects.log: The Elder tells you, briefly. You wish he had been vaguer.

events.text: The third lesson is not taught at the pavilion but on the open sky-bridge, where no one can overhear: how to take a name away from the world, from the Rolls, from the lips of the living, until even the cranes forget. Elder Gyeol speaks it once, quietly, and then watches you instead of the clouds.

choices.text: Repeat it back, word for word

effects.log: Word for word. Something small and precious leaves the world as you do, and neither of you says what.

choices.text: Say you need time before you use it

effects.log: He nods. "Everyone does. Few of them take it."

events.text: A boatman's child brings you a slip of grey silk with a rival's name on it and the seal of the Court of the Unrisen. The Court does not say why. It rarely does. It pays in cold qi from the Sea of Clouds, and it keeps a long memory for those who decline.

choices.text: Send a wonhon after the name

effects.log: The slip goes into the lantern, and the lantern goes dark. The Court will be pleased.

choices.text: Return the slip unread

effects.log: You return it with a polite note. The child shivers at the cold on your fingers.

events.text: A jar arrives with no sender, sealed in grey silk, cold as the deep clouds in winter. That is the Court's payment, and the Court's way of saying the matter is closed. Nobody thanks you. The cranes keep well clear of your terrace for a week.

choices.text: Drink what is in it

effects.log: It is the clearest water you have ever tasted, and your qi runs colder for a while.

choices.text: Pour it on the cord instead

effects.log: The cord drinks greedily. You do not like how glad it looks.

events.text: You choose a lantern-jetty at the edge of the Isles, as you were taught, and tie the name on with a thread of your own hair. The wonhon that slips off the rope was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}. It has never heard of {crt_name}. You tell it, twice, and it listens, and goes.

choices.text: Walk away without looking back

effects.log: You walk the long causeway home. The lanterns along it burn a shade lower than before.

choices.text: Say the name a third time, so it cannot lose its way

effects.log: Three times, and the jetty creaks as if a weight has stepped aboard.

events.text: A grudge of the Isles is sent from the Bell Pavilion rooftop, at moonrise, as the Cloud-Knot asks. The wonhon you give the name to was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}, and it drifts off toward {crt_name} like smoke finding a window. You feel the rope go slack, and a small bright hunger go with it.

choices.text: Count the bells until it is out of hearing

effects.log: Seven bells. The rope hangs empty. You tell yourself it is only rope.

choices.text: Follow it in thought as far as you can

effects.log: You see a pavilion, a terrace, a hand on a cup. Then the thread snaps.

events.text: You send the grudge at an elder of another house, which is a harder knot than a rival's. The wonhon from the rope was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}; you give it {crt_name} and a direction, and it goes with a sound like a tea-kettle forgetting itself.

choices.text: Seal the knot and wash your hands

effects.log: The water runs grey for a moment, then clears.

choices.text: Mark the day in your private register

effects.log: Dates are a way of owning what you have done. You write it small.

events.text: Someone of high standing, a seat of the Isles or the Ministries, is the name on the cord. The wonhon you send was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}. It hesitates at the weight of {crt_name}, and then it goes, because the knot is tied well and the Court of the Unrisen taught you to tie it.

choices.text: Breathe out, slowly

effects.log: It leaves you lighter and somehow lonelier. You do not mention either.

choices.text: Tell yourself it was only a test of the rite

effects.log: The cord does not believe you, but the cord has no one to tell.

events.text: It is not done at a jetty but at a naming-stone where the Isles register their children. You say {crt_name} to the wonhon, and then the names of {crt_his} house, every one you can recall, and one by one the lanterns on the quay go out. By dawn the stone remembers nobody.

choices.text: Scrape the stone clean afterwards

effects.log: You scrape until your nails ache. The stone stays blank in the one place you had meant to leave it.

choices.text: Leave it as it is, and go

effects.log: The stone stays blank. You do not look back, and your steps echo more than they should.

events.text: Your news of {crt_name} comes secondhand, as it should: {crt_His} garden pool has gone bitter, and {crt_his} crane will not leave the roost. {crt_He} has dreamed three nights of a figure standing at the foot of the bed with a grey rope. Nobody on the Isles has yet connected it with you.

choices.text: Send a little more of yourself after it

effects.log: A second thread, finer than the first. The omen thickens by morning.

choices.text: Take tea at the same tea-house and watch

effects.log: You watch {crt_him} pass, hollow-eyed. The tea is excellent and you finish none of it.

events.text: The elder's pavilion has started to complain: tiles crack in the night, the lantern oil sours, the servants ask to be moved. {crt_name} blames old age. A rumour reaches you that the elder has hired a mudang from a lower isle to sweep the rafters. It will not be enough.

choices.text: Let the grudge find its own pace

effects.log: It finds one. The news arrives in thin, steady drips.

choices.text: Walk past the pavilion and look up

effects.log: The roof-ridge sags in a way no wind explains. You walk on faster than you meant to.

events.text: Even high seats show omens. {crt_name} is seen to start at nothing, to refuse a cup, to leave a banquet early with a pale face. The retinue whispers. You hear all of it from a cloud-courier who has no idea what he is telling, and who is paid generously to forget.

choices.text: Pay for more news

effects.log: The courier delivers a little more, and a little more. It is a kind of company.

choices.text: Stop listening

effects.log: You stop, with effort. The silence is louder than the courier was.

events.text: {crt_name} has lost a whole rung between one season and the next, the way a pavilion loses its warmth. Neighbours have stopped calling. {crt_His} {crt_rel}, {crt_kin}, goes from healer to healer across the Isles. A letter from the Grey Cloud asks if you wish to press on, and encloses a sheet of death qi to help.

choices.text: Say you cannot help, and hand it back

effects.log: The sheet goes back unopened. Something in you unclenches, and something else sulks.

choices.text: Keep the sheet, for the rope to read

effects.log: The rope drinks the sheet down. {crt_name} will lose another rung before the leaves turn.

events.text: An elder of the Isles has taken to resting in the afternoon, then in the morning, then not rising. The house tells visitors it is a fashionable lassitude. {crt_name} sent away the last physician. The rope on your terrace is humming, quietly, like a pot that has not yet boiled.

choices.text: Let it hum

effects.log: It hums for weeks. You grow used to the sound, which is the worst of it.

choices.text: Feed it a little death qi

effects.log: The humming deepens. It sounds like agreement.

events.text: A seat of the Isles weakens in plain view. {crt_name} misses a council, then two. The Ministries send a physician who goes pale at the door and leaves without a fee. It is possible that nobody connects this to a cord on a quiet terrace. It is also possible that somebody does.

choices.text: Watch the council rolls

effects.log: Absences, written in neat ink. Each one is a small coin dropped into your account.

choices.text: Look away

effects.log: You look at your cranes instead. One of them looks back.

events.text: {crt_name} has climbed to the Lotus Cloister on the Salt-Wind Isle, and Abbess Haeun has looked at the shadow {crt_he} casts, and sent everyone else out. For forty-nine days the nuns have chanted without rest. You feel the rope tighten and then slacken, like a fisherman's line when something large turns away.

choices.text: Pour death qi after it, and pull

effects.log: You pull until your arms shake. The chanting falters once, and recovers.

choices.text: Hold still, and let it hold or not

effects.log: You hold. The chant rises and falls. You learn what patience costs.

choices.text: Call it back while you still can

effects.log: The rope comes in, hand over hand, wet and grey. The chanting stops at once.

events.text: Mudang Arin of the lantern boats has been sent for. She comes to {crt_name}'s pavilion at dusk with her fan closed and sits on the step with her back to the doorway, as one sits with a frightened animal. The rope on your terrace spasms. Something cold on the other end is being coaxed, patiently, to let go.

choices.text: Pour death qi after it, and pull

effects.log: The rope fights back harder than you expected. Somewhere, a fan opens.

choices.text: Hold still, and let it hold or not

effects.log: You hold. The fan sweeps. You feel the tide turn, slowly, against you.

choices.text: Call it back while you still can

effects.log: The rope comes home like a tired dog. A fan folds, far away.

events.text: Warden Seo Dalim of the Celestial Ministries has been told, in the way these things are told, that something is eating at {crt_name}. The Warden arrives with a seal-staff and a handful of Ministry clerks who know better than to ask questions. The rope trembles in your hand. A ministry bell is ringing, three isles away, and each stroke hurts.

choices.text: Pour death qi after it, and pull

effects.log: The bell falters and recovers. You feel the Ministry seal flare on the far end.

choices.text: Hold still, and let it hold or not

effects.log: You hold. The bell rings. You count the strokes and lose count.

choices.text: Call it back while you still can

effects.log: The rope comes in with a snap. Far away, the bell stops mid-stroke.

events.text: {crt_name} fights it alone, by sheer force of will, standing barefoot on the pavilion roof in the rain with {crt_his} arms spread wide. The rope on your terrace bucks. Whatever else {crt_he} may be, this is not a rival who gives up. The wonhon wails, and the wail comes down the cord into your palm.

choices.text: Pour death qi after it, and pull

effects.log: You pull. The wail breaks, then rises, then breaks again.

choices.text: Hold still, and let it hold or not

effects.log: You hold. Rain, wail, rope. None of the three gives way.

choices.text: Call it back while you still can

effects.log: The wail goes up one last time and stops. The rope is quiet and wet in your palm.

events.text: It holds. Word reaches you by way of a tired physician: {crt_name} has been sent home from the Cloister with kindly words and a recipe for barley tea. Everything that could be done has been done. The rope hangs quiet, and your terrace feels like a stage after the play.

choices.text: Coil it up and go to bed

effects.log: You coil it. It is lighter than it was, and you sleep badly.

choices.text: Make an offering at the jetty

effects.log: A few spirit-grains on the water. The cranes watch from a distance.

events.text: {crt_kin}, {crt_rel} of {crt_name}, has found out who you are. It took {crt_khim} four years and most of what the house had left. {crt_kHe} does not come with a sword. {crt_kHe} comes on foot to your terrace, with a small chest of spirit stones, and kneels on the wet planks. "Call it back," {crt_khe} says. "That is all I came to say."

choices.text: Take the stones, and call it back

effects.log: The stones are counted twice and the rope comes in. Nobody on the Isles will speak of this.

choices.text: Call it back, and leave the chest where it is

effects.log: You call it back. The chest stays by the door until the kneeler stops looking at it.

choices.text: Shut the door

effects.log: The latch clicks. Beyond the screen, someone is very still for a very long time.

events.text: {crt_name} has not left bed since the first frost of the high isles. Three people still visit. {crt_He} no longer asks what is wrong. The other evening, they say, {crt_he} asked after you, of all people, and smiled in a way that frightened the nurse. The rope on your terrace is very quiet.

choices.text: Let it finish

effects.log: You let it. The rope thins, then is gone.

choices.text: Stop here, and leave {crt_him} alive with what is left

effects.log: You stop. It is a half-mercy, and you know it.

choices.text: Offer it: swear the oath, and live

effects.log: You swear on the grey stone. The knot closes round both of you.

choices.text: Call it back, even now

effects.log: You call it back. It comes slowly, as if it too was tired.

events.text: An elder of the Isles, once feared, is dying slowly in a pavilion where no one raises their voice. {crt_name} has stopped receiving letters. The healers have quit. At the foot of the bed a grey rope that only you can see is drawn tight as a bow. One more pull, or one release.

choices.text: Let it finish

effects.log: You let it. The pavilion goes quiet, and stays so.

choices.text: Stop here, and leave {crt_him} alive with what is left

effects.log: You ease the rope. The elder lives, a husk of reputation.

choices.text: Offer it: swear the oath, and live

effects.log: The knot closes round both of you.

choices.text: Call it back, even now

effects.log: It comes, like a tide going out. The elder sleeps, at last.

events.text: A seat of the Isles lies on the edge. The Ministries have quietly drafted a successor. {crt_name} knows, in the way the dying know, that the rope is tied to a person and not an accident. The next dawn will decide it, and only your hand is on the cord.

choices.text: Let it finish

effects.log: It finishes. The Ministries announce the succession at noon.

choices.text: Stop here, and leave {crt_him} alive with what is left

effects.log: You stop. The seat will be passed to another, and {crt_name} will live to watch.

choices.text: Offer it: swear the oath, and live

effects.log: The oath closes. You feel a great weight take its seat on your shoulders.

choices.text: Call it back, even now

effects.log: The rope goes slack. {crt_name} wakes at dawn and asks for tea.

events.text: They bury {crt_name} on a clear morning from the high terraces. You attend; a mudang of the Isles has every reason to. Nobody at the graveside knows yet. You perform the rites, since nobody asked another, and you are very good. {crt_kin} thanks you with red eyes. A servant presses a small purse of favours into your hand.

choices.text: Take the favours

effects.log: The purse is light and heavy at once. You do not count it.

choices.text: Stay behind, and tidy the grave

effects.log: You sweep the stones until dusk. Nobody sees you do it, which is the point.

events.text: You stop it there. {crt_name} wakes one morning with the cold gone from the pavilion, and lies a long time before daring to breathe in. {crt_He} is alive, with a third of what {crt_he} had. The isle goes on whispering about a mysterious decline. You do not correct the isle.

choices.text: Send a small gift, with no name on it

effects.log: A basket of barley cakes, sent through a stranger. {crt_name} eats them, and does not ask.

choices.text: Put it out of your mind

effects.log: You manage it for a month. Then the month ends.

events.text: The elder survives, thin and silent, and gives up the post a season later with a dignified little speech nobody quite believes. {crt_kin} will inherit. You watch from a distance as the house is slowly reorganised around a person who no longer leaves the pavilion.

choices.text: Send a sealed note of respect

effects.log: No signature. The elder reads it twice and burns it.

choices.text: Leave it alone

effects.log: You do, and mostly succeed.

events.text: The seat survives, but not the person: {crt_name} resigns from the Ministries on grounds of health and moves to a quiet isle with a single servant. A lesser relative takes the chair. The papers do not mention you. The cord on your terrace is gone grey with disuse.

choices.text: Send a courier with grain

effects.log: The courier returns with an empty sack and a bow. Nothing else.

choices.text: Look at the rope and say nothing

effects.log: It lies there like a sleeping snake.

events.text: You call it back, hand over hand, for a night and a day. It does not want to come. It was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}, and you gave it somewhere to go, and now you are telling it to stop. It comes because you ask, and because the rope is stronger than its grief. It leaves a cold stain across your palm.

choices.text: Burn incense for the wonhon

effects.log: Grey smoke rises through the lanterns. You say its old name once.

choices.text: Keep it from Elder Gyeol

effects.log: A small lie, told to a person who tells larger ones. It sits easier than expected.

events.text: The wonhon returns early. You feel it come along the causeway, puzzled, like a dog sent to fetch someone from an emptied house. {crt_name} is out of its reach now, and not by any art of yours. The rope trembles for a moment and then lies still.

choices.text: Take it back on the rope

effects.log: It comes easily, relieved to be called by a familiar voice.

choices.text: Laugh, since there is nobody else to

effects.log: You laugh. The cranes startle and rise, then settle.

events.text: It comes back at the third bell. You know it at once and have just time to set down your cup. Someone has cut it, with a sutra or a song or simply by being tired of fear, and now everything it was holds against you, cold, through the rope. The Bell Pavilion is three isles away and you can hear it ringing.

choices.text: Go to Spirit-Mother Hwaseon for the cleansing gut

effects.log: She makes you wait three days on the jetty, then cleanses you with salt and silence.

choices.text: Fight it off by your own name

effects.log: You say your name and your lineage, loudly, to the empty terrace. It hurts, and it works, mostly.

choices.text: Listen to what it has to say

effects.log: It speaks for an hour in a voice you almost know. You come away changed.

events.text: A great grudge rebounds like a boat swamped in a squall. It was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}, and it comes home to you with every wrong it ever carried, faster than you can lift the rope. The cranes scatter. The lanterns of Ghost-Reed Isle are lit, one by one, as if someone is walking through them.

choices.text: Go to Spirit-Mother Hwaseon for the cleansing gut

effects.log: She takes the stain with her bare hands. It will take months to fade.

choices.text: Fight it off by your own name

effects.log: You stand your ground. It costs you a good deal.

choices.text: Listen to what it has to say

effects.log: It is much louder than you expected and has much to say.

events.text: Mudang Arin comes herself. She walks up the hill from the lantern boats with her fan closed and sits on your step. You knew she would. "That one cried, you know," she says, "when I let it go. {crt_who}. It asked me why nobody had thought to ask it first." She does not say whether she means the wonhon or you.

choices.text: Ask her how you look

effects.log: "Tired," she says. "Like all of us who talk to the dead for a living." It is the kindest thing anyone has said all season.

choices.text: Tell her to go home

effects.log: She goes, unhurried. The step stays warm where she sat.

events.text: Spirit-Mother Hwaseon knows. Nobody told her. A strip of straw rope hangs across the door of the inner room now, and she gives your lesson on the porch in the same voice as ever. As you leave she says, without turning: "Whatever you owe the dead, child, do not pay it in other people's years."

choices.text: Bow, and say nothing

effects.log: You bow. The straw rope sways without wind.

choices.text: Tell her the Pavilion never paid anyone back for any grief

effects.log: She stops. "No," she says. "It never did." It is not a concession.

events.text: It takes {crt_kin}, {crt_rel} of {crt_name}, some years to become what {crt_khe} needed to be. {crt_kHe} has done it. {crt_kHe} waits at the ferry landing when you come down with your bell, and you can see from the way the light moves on the water that {crt_khe} came alone.

choices.text: Meet {crt_khim} at the landing

ok.log: You win, and it is not a victory. {crt_kin} drops to one knee, breathing hard. You walk away with a bruise you will keep.

fail.log: The landing tilts and you go into the cold water. When you surface {crt_kin} is gone, and your bell is gone with {crt_khim}.

choices.text: Put your bell down in the water, and tell {crt_khim} it is over

effects.log: The bell sinks. {crt_kin} watches the ripples, and neither of you moves for a long time.

choices.text: Slip away across the water by night

effects.log: You slip off on a night barge. The landing stays in your mind.

events.text: You tie it where their road crosses yours: a cord of five colours with the wonhon wound in it, knotted three times. {crt_name} stops with a cup halfway to {crt_his} lips. {crt_He} does not know what has happened. {crt_He} only knows that the tea has gone cold in the hand, and that something in the room is listening.

choices.text: Send {crt_him} a note, so that {crt_he} knows

effects.log: A single line in grey ink. By nightfall the whole isle knows that {crt_name} has been marked.

choices.text: Tell nobody, and wait

effects.log: The waiting is the real rite. It lasts a month.

events.text: You knot the cord round your own wrist as well, as the oath requires, and the wonhon sinks into the weave. Whatever happens to the knot happens to you. {crt_name}, far away, drops a bowl and does not know why. You look at your wrist, and the cord looks back.

choices.text: Keep your hands very still

effects.log: You keep them still for an hour. The cord goes quiet, as a sleeper might.

choices.text: Test the knot with one gentle pull

effects.log: A far bowl rattles. You regret the test.

events.text: A limit is the cruellest kind of knot: it caps what a person can become. You tie it to {crt_name} and feel the ceiling lower, one rung at a time. From now on {crt_he} will climb only so far, and not know why.

choices.text: Pull the knot tight

effects.log: Tight. You feel a small, cold satisfaction, and hate it.

choices.text: Loosen it by a hair

effects.log: A hair is not much. It is still something.

events.text: The cord slips on the third knot. {crt_name} wakes with a mark on the wrist and the taste of cold river in the mouth, and is on {crt_his} feet at once, and knows exactly which direction to look. The mark glows grey for an hour, then fades. You have made an enemy who knows you are an enemy.

choices.text: Soothe the rope and burn the cord

effects.log: The cord burns grey. The rope sulks for a week.

choices.text: Keep the cord for another time

effects.log: You coil it away. It is not finished with you.

events.text: {crt_name} tried. {crt_He} was always going to, and you have often wondered what it would look like. It looks like someone in the middle of a room, in the middle of a sentence, who sits down very suddenly. The knot tightens round your own chest as well. Somewhere on the Isles a bowl is dropped.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let the knot rest

effects.log: It rests. You breathe shallowly, and it rests a little longer.

choices.text: Untie it, before anyone else has to see this

effects.log: You untie it with shaking hands. It comes loose like wet silk.

choices.text: Draw it closed

effects.log: You draw it. The rope goes still. So do you, for a while.

events.text: The limit bit back. {crt_name} reached for the next rung and the ceiling pushed; both of you felt it. A rattle in the house, a stumble on the stair. Somewhere, a servant says the master has turned the colour of old paper. You press a hand to your own chest, and the pressure matches.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let the knot rest

effects.log: Rest. You sit very still and wait for the knot to calm.

choices.text: Untie it, before anyone else has to see this

effects.log: The knot loosens. The weight lifts from both of you.

choices.text: Draw it closed

effects.log: The limit hardens. You feel it set, and wish you had not.

events.text: Somebody has told {crt_name} how it is done. Perhaps Mudang Arin; perhaps an old scroll; perhaps only a hot needle, a cup of strong wine and a great deal of wanting to. The knot is cut. You know because you are on the floor, and your hands are open, and the rope lies in two grey pieces on the terrace.

choices.text: Get up. There is a great deal to do now

effects.log: You get up. The terrace spins and settles. The work ahead is long.

choices.text: Lie there a little longer

effects.log: The planks are cool. You think about what the knot meant, and what it cost.

events.text: {crt_name} reached the next rung this winter. You knew before anyone. It lasted about as long as a breath out, and then the knot took it back, the whole gain, between one heartbeat and the next. The house is baffled. You are not, and you sit very still, hating how well it works.

choices.text: Let {crt_him} try again

effects.log: The next attempt comes in spring. The knot is waiting.

choices.text: Send {crt_him} a good healer, at your own cost

effects.log: Your favours pay for the healer. {crt_name} never learns who sent the visit.

events.text: {crt_name} has sent a gift for the new year. {crt_He} sends one every year, and always on time. This year it is a jar of plum wine and a letter, in a beautiful hand, hoping that you are in good health. You turn the letter over and over. It is the most dangerous thing in the house.

choices.text: Keep the wine for a guest

effects.log: Your guests say it is wonderful wine. You sleep soundly anyway, which is its own kind of insult.

choices.text: Pour it out on the ground, to be safe

effects.log: The ground drinks it without complaint. You feel foolish and relieved.

events.text: It takes as long to untie as it took to tie, and then the same again, because your hands have got to know what they are doing and to mean it. At dawn the cord comes apart, and it is only cord. {crt_name} wakes somewhere on the Isles and does not know why {crt_he} is smiling. The cranes land on your terrace for the first time in a year.

choices.text: Burn the cord

effects.log: Grey smoke, one thin line, going straight up.

choices.text: Keep the cord, to remember

effects.log: It sits in a drawer, harmless as old thread.

events.text: {crt_name} went down to breakfast this spring and asked the person across the table, with great courtesy, who they were. Thirty years, those two. {crt_He} says it is a very kind face. {crt_He} knows every other face on the Isles, and not this one. The healers call it a fashionable forgetting. You know the name for it.

choices.text: Go and hear it for yourself

effects.log: You go. It is exactly as described, and worse in the details.

choices.text: Do not go. You know how it goes

effects.log: You stay home. The clouds go by. You have never seen so many.

events.text: {crt_kin} has reached the Bell Pavilion, footsore, the label still stitched to {crt_khis} coat. {crt_kHe} accuses nobody. {crt_kHe} has heard you know old curses, and sets out what the house can pay for the cure. It is a good deal. It is also exactly what you would have asked.

choices.text: Tell {crt_khim} the cure, and call it back

effects.log: You tell it all, and mean it. {crt_kin} writes it down in a shaking hand.

choices.text: Name a price for what you know

effects.log: A price is named. {crt_kin} pays it without a word, and leaves without one.

choices.text: Say you know of no such cure

effects.log: You say it flatly. {crt_kin} looks at you for a moment and nods.

events.text: {crt_kin} is back, and no longer polite. {crt_kHe} has been to the Lotus Cloister and to Mudang Arin, and lays on your table a sheet with four names, three crossed out. "She says it would have to be you," {crt_khe} says. {crt_kHe} has a spirit-sword at {crt_khis} belt, and has not touched it yet.

choices.text: Give {crt_khim} the cure, and be done

effects.log: You tell it. The sword stays in its sheath, and the relief is a physical thing.

choices.text: Sell it, at a price that hurts

effects.log: You name a price that makes {crt_kin} flinch. {crt_kHe} pays.

choices.text: Look at the sword, and say nothing

effects.log: The silence stretches. {crt_kin} does not draw.

events.text: First frost. {crt_kin} stands on the causeway below the Pavilion, the label gone grey with weather, a spirit-sword in both hands. {crt_kHe} has come to take the cure out of you, whichever way it can be taken. {crt_kHe} looks very tired and very certain.

choices.text: Go down the causeway to meet {crt_khim}

ok.log: You knock the blade aside and hold {crt_khim} still until the fight leaves {crt_khim}. It leaves slowly.

fail.log: The blade bites. {crt_kin} does not finish it. You are left on the causeway, breathing, while a figure walks away.

choices.text: Walk down with empty hands, and give {crt_khim} the cure

effects.log: You hold out empty hands. The sword lowers. The relief on that face is terrible to see.

choices.text: Sell it to {crt_khim}, even now

effects.log: Even now. {crt_kin} pays, hollow-eyed. You do not look back.

events.text: It comes back to {crt_name} in the middle of a meal, they say, or it comes back in part. {crt_He} puts down {crt_his} cup and looks across the table, and says a name. Nobody at that table moves. The name is correct. Somewhere on the Isles a rope goes slack, and a long-held breath leaves a long-held house.

choices.text: Stay away. This is theirs

effects.log: You stay away. It is the hardest thing you have done this year.

choices.text: Go and watch it from the causeway

effects.log: You watch from a distance. Nobody sees you. It is bittersweet.

events.text: One spring {crt_name} walks out of the pavilion gate in good spirits and asks a boatman the way to {crt_his} own house. Nobody sees {crt_him} again, unless you count the stories: a courteous old person on the quays, who knows everyone and is known by none. You count the stories. You count them often.

choices.text: Say the name of {crt_name} once, for the record

effects.log: One name, aloud, to nobody. The wind takes it.

choices.text: Forget about it. You are good at that

effects.log: You are. It is a little too easy.

events.text: You wake, and across the table is a kind and tired face you have known for years. You open your mouth to say good morning, and you stop. In a lantern-market, far away, a pleasant stranger writes something in a ledger, and the ink glows briefly grey. You have, you realise, lost a name of your own.

choices.text: Say nothing, and start writing things down

effects.log: You write everything. It is not enough. It is never enough.

choices.text: Say good morning, anyway

effects.log: The face smiles. You do not know whose it is, and it does not seem to matter.

events.text: A warden in grey, Seo Dalim of the Celestial Ministries, sits down in the outer yard of the Bell Pavilion and asks for a cup of water. He drinks it. He looks at your rope, counts its knots aloud, and then counts the places where a rope of that size ought to have been cut. "Mudang," he says, "I have only one question."

choices.text: Say you are a poor mudang, and offer more water

effects.log: You offer more water. He drinks it, and says nothing, which is worse.

choices.text: Tell him you have given it up. And do

effects.log: You say it, and then you mean it, between one breath and the next.

choices.text: Tell him who it is he is talking to

effects.log: He nods slowly. The yard goes quiet. You have crossed a line, and you know it.

events.text: Warden Seo stops you on the ferry road, in rain, at a place where neither bank can see. He must have planned that for your benefit, you think, and not for his. He unties the cord from your wrist with two fingers, as one handles a dead mouse, and lays a Ministry seal on your palm. "Choose," he says.

choices.text: Try to stop him

ok.log: You stop him, barely. He steps back, bows, and does not draw his seal-staff. Not today.

fail.log: The seal-staff finds your ribs. You go to the ground and he steps over you without a word.

choices.text: Hold out your rope, and renounce it all

effects.log: You hold it out. He takes it, and for a moment looks almost sorry.

choices.text: Get away over the river

ok.log: You are across the river before he has finished speaking. The rain hides everything.

fail.log: You slip on the wet bank and the river takes your boots and your pride.

events.text: He has grown old on your account. You had not thought of it until you see him at the foot of the Pavilion stair, one hand on a staff, the seal-staff on his back grey with handling. He has come alone, which is a courtesy and a threat. "It is only you and I, now," Seo Dalim says. "Let us settle it."

choices.text: Come down, and finish it

ok.log: You come down. It is a long and weary fight, and in the end you stand where the warden stood, and the Pavilion goes quiet behind you.

fail.log: He seals you, gently, with a hand that knows exactly where to press. The rope goes dead, and so do your arms.

choices.text: Come down, and hand him the rites

effects.log: You hand over the cords, the slips, the little book. He weighs them, and nods.

events.text: It is done, and done properly. Nothing you could point to: your hands work, and the rope is only a rope, and the dead still come to you with their griefs. But when you reach for the old cold, nothing answers. It is like reaching for a stair that has been taken away. You stand there a long moment with your hand out.

choices.text: Go on being a mudang, since it seems you still are

effects.log: The dead still come. You listen to them with an unfamiliar, plain gentleness.

choices.text: Throw the cup into the sea of clouds

effects.log: It falls a very long way. You do not hear it land.

events.text: You walk up the hill with all of it: the cords, the slips, the little book of hours and stairways. Spirit-Mother Hwaseon is at the top, cutting reeds, the lamps already lit. She takes it from you, piece by piece, as one takes laundry from a child. When she has the last she sets it all on the fire and says, "Sit. Eat. You are very thin."

choices.text: Sit, and eat

effects.log: You eat reed-bread and drink bitter tea. It is the best meal you have had in years.

choices.text: Ask how long it takes

effects.log: "All your life," she says. "I will teach you the first part."

events.text: Somebody says the name of {crt_name} in the lantern market, and you turn your head before you can think. You can no longer hear it without a slight pull at the wrist, the way a kite tugs when there is no wind. The speaker moves on, never knowing. You stand there with your arm half-raised.

choices.text: Think about something else

effects.log: You do, with effort. The pull fades, slowly, like a bell dying.

choices.text: Let yourself think about it

effects.log: You let it in. It comes in warmly, and sits down.

events.text: As a child you would not let anyone tie a thread around your wrist, not even for a birthday. Now you pass a shrine on the Isles with its five-coloured cords in the wind, and a coldness goes through you from a life you cannot remember. Your hand knows a knot your mind does not. A crane watches from the railing.

choices.text: Leave an offering, for whoever it was

effects.log: A handful of rice on the rail. The crane takes a grain, delicately.

choices.text: Remember how the knot goes

effects.log: Your fingers do the rest. When you look down there is a perfect knot in a scrap of thread.

events.text: A younger kin of {crt_name} comes to the ferry landing of the isle and asks every boatman about a mudang who knows old curses. The boatmen shake their heads and look at their oars. {crt_kin} gets as far as your door by evening, and knocks, and says very quietly, "Please."

choices.text: Tell {crt_khim} the cure, and call it back

effects.log: You tell it, plainly. The knocking stops, and the quiet afterwards is kind.

choices.text: Name a price for what you know

effects.log: You name it. {crt_kin} pays it without a word.

choices.text: Say you know of no such cure

effects.log: The door stays shut. Footsteps go away down the stairs.

events.text: The Hollow Saint Mugwan of the Choir of Unanswered Prayers is waiting at the edge of your temple's lamplight, a figure the incense does not touch. "You keep prayers on a shelf like preserves," the Saint says. "Some of them are owed an answer. The Choir teaches how to answer with a writ."

choices.text: Ask what it costs

effects.log: The Saint says nothing, and the lamps lean toward the silence.

choices.text: Say you will think about it

effects.log: The Saint bows to the edge of the dark. "Think on the night of a dead moon," comes the soft answer. "We hear best then."

events.text: On a cracked altar-step the Saint lets you hold the writ-cord. A curse, says the Hollow Saint, is only a prayer turned around. Give a wonhon the name of a rival god, and let the Writ of Bent Fate carry it. Your fingers tremble on the cord, and the cord does not seem to object.

choices.text: Practise on the cord until your hands steady

effects.log: Hour after hour on the cold step. By dusk the tremor is gone, and you wish it had stayed.

choices.text: Ask what became of the last pupil

effects.log: The Saint looks at the dark. "Answered," comes the reply. You decide not to ask how.

events.text: The second lesson is a knot between two names, pulled tight with a vow. The Hollow Saint calls it the Knot-Oath: what binds a foe binds you. "Mind the weight," the Saint says, placing a black pebble in your palm. The pebble is heavier than a pebble should be, and warmer.

choices.text: Tie it on the pebble until it holds

effects.log: It holds on the ninth try. You feel the oath settle beneath your ribs like a second pulse.

choices.text: Ask what happens if the knot is cut

effects.log: The Saint tells you, briefly. You wish it had been vaguer.

events.text: The third lesson is given on the empty ferry-pier, where no one can overhear: how to take a name out of the world, out of the Book of Fates, off the lips of the faithful, until even the shrines forget. The Hollow Saint says it once, quietly, and watches you instead of the water.

choices.text: Repeat it back, word for word

effects.log: Word for word. Something small and precious leaves the world as you do, and neither of you says what.

choices.text: Say you need time before you use it

effects.log: The Saint nods. "All do. Few take it."

events.text: A temple sprite brings a scrap of black cloth with a rival god's name on it and the mark of the Choir. The Choir does not say why. It rarely does. It pays in cold faith from the unanswered, and it keeps a long memory for those who decline.

choices.text: Send a wonhon after the name

effects.log: The scrap burns in the lamp without smoke. The Choir will be pleased.

choices.text: Return the scrap unread

effects.log: You return it with a polite word. The sprite shivers at the cold on your fingers.

events.text: A flask arrives with no sender, sealed in black cloth, cold as a river in the underworld. That is the Choir's payment, and the Choir's way of saying the matter is closed. Nobody thanks you. The temple hound will not come near the altar for a week.

choices.text: Drink what is in it

effects.log: It is the clearest water you have ever tasted, and your divinity runs colder for a while.

choices.text: Pour it on the cord instead

effects.log: The cord drinks greedily. You do not like how glad it looks.

events.text: You choose a ferry-landing at the edge of the heavens, as you were taught, and tie the name on with a hair of your own. The wonhon that slips off the cord was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}. It has never heard of {crt_name}. You tell it, twice, and it listens, and goes.

choices.text: Walk away without looking back

effects.log: You walk the long pier home. The lamps along it burn a shade lower than before.

choices.text: Say the name a third time, so it cannot lose its way

effects.log: Three times, and the planks creak as if a weight has stepped aboard.

events.text: A writ of bent fate is sent from your temple roof at moonrise. The wonhon you give the name to was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}, and it drifts toward {crt_name} like smoke finding a window. You feel the cord go slack, and a small bright hunger go with it.

choices.text: Count the bells until it is out of hearing

effects.log: Seven bells. The cord hangs empty. You tell yourself it is only cord.

choices.text: Follow it in thought as far as you can

effects.log: You see a shrine, an altar, a hand on a cup. Then the thread snaps.

events.text: You send the writ at an elder god, a harder knot than a rival's. The wonhon from the cord was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}; you give it {crt_name} and a direction, and it goes with a sound like a lamp forgetting its flame.

choices.text: Seal the knot and wash your hands

effects.log: The water runs black for a moment, then clears.

choices.text: Mark the day in your private tablet

effects.log: Dates are a way of owning what you have done. You write it small.

events.text: Someone of high standing, a seat in the Heavenly Court or a throne of another pantheon, is the name on the cord. The wonhon you send was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}. It hesitates at the weight of {crt_name}, and then it goes, because the knot is tied well and the Choir taught you to tie it.

choices.text: Breathe out, slowly

effects.log: It leaves you lighter and somehow lonelier. You do not mention either.

choices.text: Tell yourself it was only a test of the rite

effects.log: The cord does not believe you, but the cord has no one to tell.

events.text: It is not done at a ferry-landing but at a naming-font where the divine register their young. You say {crt_name} to the wonhon, and then the names of {crt_his} line, every one you can recall, and one by one the votive flames along the font go out. By dawn the font remembers nobody.

choices.text: Scour the font clean afterwards

effects.log: You scour until your hands ache. The stone stays blank in the one place you meant to leave marked.

choices.text: Leave it as it is, and go

effects.log: The font stays blank. You do not look back, and your steps echo more than they should.

events.text: Your news of {crt_name} comes secondhand, as it should: {crt_His} sacred spring has gone bitter, and {crt_his} temple hound will not leave the sanctum. {crt_He} has dreamed three nights of a figure at the foot of the altar with a black cord. No one in the heavens has yet connected it with you.

choices.text: Send a little more of yourself after it

effects.log: A second thread, finer than the first. The omen thickens by morning.

choices.text: Take a cup at the same shrine and watch

effects.log: You watch {crt_him} pass, hollow-eyed. The offering is fine and you finish none of it.

events.text: The elder god's temple has begun to complain: tiles crack in the night, the lamp oil sours, the attendants ask to be moved. {crt_name} blames age. A rumour says an acolyte from a lower shrine has been hired to sweep the rafters. It will not be enough.

choices.text: Let the writ find its own pace

effects.log: It finds one. The news arrives in thin, steady drips.

choices.text: Walk past the temple and look up

effects.log: The roof-beam sags in a way no wind explains. You walk on faster than you meant to.

events.text: Even high thrones show omens. {crt_name} is seen to start at nothing, to refuse an offering, to leave a feast early with a pale face. The retinue whispers. You hear it from a messenger-bird who has no idea what she is telling, and is paid well to forget.

choices.text: Pay for more news

effects.log: The bird delivers a little more, and a little more. It is a kind of company.

choices.text: Stop listening

effects.log: You stop, with effort. The silence is louder than the bird was.

events.text: {crt_name} has lost a whole rung between one season and the next, the way a shrine loses its warmth. Fellow gods have stopped calling. {crt_His} {crt_rel}, {crt_kin}, goes from healer to healer across the heavens. A note from the Choir asks if you wish to press on, and encloses a leaf of black faith to help.

choices.text: Say you cannot help, and hand it back

effects.log: The leaf goes back unopened. Something in you unclenches, and something else sulks.

choices.text: Keep the leaf, for the cord to read

effects.log: The cord drinks the leaf down. {crt_name} will lose another rung before the festival.

events.text: An elder god has taken to resting in the afternoon, then in the morning, then not rising. The temple tells visitors it is a fashionable lassitude. {crt_name} sent away the last physician. The cord in your sanctum is humming, quietly, like a bowl that has not yet rung.

choices.text: Let it hum

effects.log: It hums for weeks. You grow used to the sound, which is the worst of it.

choices.text: Feed it a little black faith

effects.log: The humming deepens. It sounds like agreement.

events.text: A throne weakens in plain view. {crt_name} misses a council, then two. The Heavenly Court sends a physician who goes pale at the door and leaves without a fee. It is possible that nobody connects this to a cord in a quiet sanctum. It is also possible that somebody does.

choices.text: Watch the council rolls

effects.log: Absences, written in neat ink. Each one is a small coin dropped into your account.

choices.text: Look away

effects.log: You look at your hound instead. It looks back.

events.text: {crt_name} has climbed to the Quiet Temple, and Keeper Hanbit has looked at the shadow {crt_he} casts, and sent every other priest out. For forty-nine days the temple has chanted without rest. You feel the cord tighten, then slacken, like a line when something large turns away.

choices.text: Pour black faith after it, and pull

effects.log: You pull until your arms shake. The chanting falters once, and recovers.

choices.text: Hold still, and let it hold or not

effects.log: You hold. The chant rises and falls. You learn what patience costs.

choices.text: Call it back while you still can

effects.log: The cord comes in, hand over hand, wet and black. The chanting stops at once.

events.text: Ferry-priestess Dalrae has been sent for. She comes to {crt_name}'s sanctum at dusk with her ladle closed in her fist and sits on the step with her back to the door, as one sits with a frightened animal. The cord in your hand spasms. Something cold on the other end is being coaxed, patiently, to let go.

choices.text: Pour black faith after it, and pull

effects.log: The cord fights back harder than you expected. Somewhere, a ladle rings.

choices.text: Hold still, and let it hold or not

effects.log: You hold. The ladle sweeps. You feel the tide turn, slowly, against you.

choices.text: Call it back while you still can

effects.log: The cord comes home like a tired hound. A ladle is set down, far away.

events.text: Bailiff Jin of the Book of Fates has been told, in the way these things are told, that something is eating at {crt_name}. The Bailiff arrives with a ledger-staff and a handful of clerks who know better than to ask. The cord trembles in your hand. A bell of the Heavenly Court is ringing, three domains away, and each stroke hurts.

choices.text: Pour black faith after it, and pull

effects.log: The bell falters and recovers. You feel the Court seal flare on the far end.

choices.text: Hold still, and let it hold or not

effects.log: You hold. The bell rings. You count the strokes and lose count.

choices.text: Call it back while you still can

effects.log: The cord comes in with a snap. Far away, the bell stops mid-stroke.

events.text: {crt_name} fights it alone, by sheer force of will, standing barefoot on the temple roof in the storm with {crt_his} arms spread wide. The cord in your sanctum bucks. Whatever else {crt_he} may be, this is not a rival who gives up. The wonhon wails, and the wail comes down the cord into your palm.

choices.text: Pour black faith after it, and pull

effects.log: You pull. The wail breaks, then rises, then breaks again.

choices.text: Hold still, and let it hold or not

effects.log: You hold. Storm, wail, cord. None of the three gives way.

choices.text: Call it back while you still can

effects.log: The wail goes up one last time and stops. The cord is quiet and wet in your palm.

events.text: It holds. Word reaches you by way of a weary healer-god: {crt_name} has been sent home with kindly words and a recipe for barley broth. Everything that could be done has been done. The cord hangs quiet, and your sanctum feels like a stage after the play.

choices.text: Coil it up and go to rest

effects.log: You coil it. It is lighter than it was, and you rest badly.

choices.text: Make an offering at the ferry-landing

effects.log: A handful of grain on the water. The temple hound watches from a distance.

events.text: {crt_kin}, {crt_rel} of {crt_name}, has found out who you are. It took {crt_khim} four ages and most of what the line had left. {crt_kHe} does not come with a spear. {crt_kHe} comes on foot to your sanctum, with a small chest of offerings, and kneels on the cold floor. "Call it back," {crt_khe} says. "That is all I came to say."

choices.text: Take the offerings, and call it back

effects.log: The offerings are counted twice and the cord comes in. No one in the heavens will speak of this.

choices.text: Call it back, and leave the chest where it is

effects.log: You call it back. The chest stays by the door until the kneeler stops looking at it.

choices.text: Shut the door

effects.log: The latch clicks. Beyond the screen, someone is very still for a very long time.

events.text: {crt_name} has not risen since the first frost of the high heavens. Three attendants still visit. {crt_He} no longer asks what is wrong. The other evening, they say, {crt_he} asked after you, of all beings, and smiled in a way that frightened the nurse. The cord in your sanctum is very quiet.

choices.text: Let it finish

effects.log: You let it. The cord thins, then is gone.

choices.text: Stop here, and leave {crt_him} alive with what is left

effects.log: You stop. It is a half-mercy, and you know it.

choices.text: Offer it: swear the oath, and live

effects.log: You swear on the black pebble. The knot closes round both of you.

choices.text: Call it back, even now

effects.log: You call it back. It comes slowly, as if it too was tired.

events.text: An elder god, once feared, is dying slowly in a temple where no one raises their voice. {crt_name} has stopped receiving messages. The healers have quit. At the foot of the bed a black cord that only you can see is drawn tight as a bow. One more pull, or one release.

choices.text: Let it finish

effects.log: You let it. The temple goes quiet, and stays so.

choices.text: Stop here, and leave {crt_him} alive with what is left

effects.log: You ease the cord. The elder lives, a husk of reputation.

choices.text: Offer it: swear the oath, and live

effects.log: The knot closes round both of you.

choices.text: Call it back, even now

effects.log: It comes, like a tide going out. The elder sleeps, at last.

events.text: A throne of the heavens lies on the edge. The Court has quietly drafted a successor. {crt_name} knows, in the way the dying know, that the cord is tied to a being and not an accident. The next dawn will decide it, and only your hand is on the cord.

choices.text: Let it finish

effects.log: It finishes. The Court announces the succession at noon.

choices.text: Stop here, and leave {crt_him} alive with what is left

effects.log: You stop. The throne will pass to another, and {crt_name} will live to watch.

choices.text: Offer it: swear the oath, and live

effects.log: The oath closes. You feel a great weight take its seat on your shoulders.

choices.text: Call it back, even now

effects.log: The cord goes slack. {crt_name} wakes at dawn and asks for nectar.

events.text: They lay {crt_name} to rest on a clear morning from the high terraces. You attend; a priest of the writ has every reason to. Nobody at the rite knows yet. You perform the offices, since nobody asked another, and you are very good. {crt_kin} thanks you with red eyes. An attendant presses a small token of favour into your hand.

choices.text: Take the token

effects.log: The token is light and heavy at once. You do not weigh it.

choices.text: Stay behind, and tidy the shrine

effects.log: You sweep the steps until dusk. Nobody sees you do it, which is the point.

events.text: You stop it there. {crt_name} wakes one morning with the cold gone from the sanctum, and lies a long time before daring to breathe in. {crt_He} is alive, with a third of what {crt_he} had. The heavens go on whispering about a mysterious decline. You do not correct the heavens.

choices.text: Send a small gift, with no name on it

effects.log: A basket of grain cakes, sent through a stranger. {crt_name} eats them, and does not ask.

choices.text: Put it out of your mind

effects.log: You manage it for a month. Then the month ends.

events.text: The elder survives, thin and silent, and gives up the office an age later with a dignified little speech nobody quite believes. {crt_kin} will inherit. You watch from a distance as the temple is slowly reorganised around a god who no longer leaves the sanctum.

choices.text: Send a sealed note of respect

effects.log: No signature. The elder reads it twice and burns it.

choices.text: Leave it alone

effects.log: You do, and mostly succeed.

events.text: The throne survives, but not the god: {crt_name} resigns from the Court on grounds of health and moves to a quiet shrine with a single attendant. A lesser relative takes the seat. The Book of Fates does not mention you. The cord in your sanctum has gone grey with disuse.

choices.text: Send a messenger with grain

effects.log: The messenger returns with an empty sack and a bow. Nothing else.

choices.text: Look at the cord and say nothing

effects.log: It lies there like a sleeping snake.

events.text: You call it back, hand over hand, for a night and a day. It does not want to come. It was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}, and you gave it somewhere to go, and now you are telling it to stop. It comes because you ask, and because the cord is stronger than its grief. It leaves a cold stain across your palm.

choices.text: Burn incense for the wonhon

effects.log: Grey smoke rises through the lamps. You say its old name once.

choices.text: Keep it from the Hollow Saint

effects.log: A small lie, told to a being who tells larger ones. It sits easier than expected.

events.text: The wonhon returns early. You feel it come along the pier, puzzled, like a hound sent to fetch someone from an emptied house. {crt_name} is out of its reach now, and not by any art of yours. The cord trembles for a moment and then lies still.

choices.text: Take it back on the cord

effects.log: It comes easily, relieved to be called by a familiar voice.

choices.text: Laugh, since there is nobody else to

effects.log: You laugh. The temple doves startle and rise, then settle.

events.text: It comes back at the third bell. You know it at once and have just time to set down your cup. Someone has cut it, with a hymn or a song or simply by being tired of fear, and now everything it was holds against you, cold, through the cord. The Ferry Landing of Baekun is three domains away and you can hear its bell.

choices.text: Go to the Ferrywoman Ok-i for the cleansing

effects.log: She makes you wait three days on the pier, then cleanses you with salt and silence.

choices.text: Fight it off by your own name

effects.log: You say your name and your domain, loudly, to the empty sanctum. It hurts, and it works, mostly.

choices.text: Listen to what it has to say

effects.log: It speaks for an hour in a voice you almost know. You come away changed.

events.text: A great grudge rebounds like a ferry swamped in a squall. It was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}, and it comes home to you with every wrong it ever carried, faster than you can lift the cord. The temple doves scatter. The lamps of the sanctum are lit, one by one, as if someone is walking through them.

choices.text: Go to the Ferrywoman Ok-i for the cleansing

effects.log: She takes the stain with her bare hands. It will take ages to fade.

choices.text: Fight it off by your own name

effects.log: You stand your ground. It costs you a good deal.

choices.text: Listen to what it has to say

effects.log: It is much louder than you expected and has much to say.

events.text: Ferry-priestess Dalrae comes herself. She walks up from the landing alone, with her ladle closed in her fist, and sits on your step. You knew she would. "That one cried, you know," she says, "when I let it go. {crt_who}. It asked me why nobody had thought to ask it first." She does not say whether she means the wonhon or you.

choices.text: Ask her how you look

effects.log: "Tired," she says. "Like all of us who talk to the dead for a living." It is the kindest thing anyone has said all age.

choices.text: Tell her to go home

effects.log: She goes, unhurried. The step stays warm where she sat.

events.text: The Ferrywoman Ok-i knows. Nobody told her. A strip of straw rope hangs across the door of the boathouse now, and she gives your lesson on the pier in the same voice as ever. As you leave she says, without turning: "Whatever you owe the dead, do not pay it in other gods' ages."

choices.text: Bow, and say nothing

effects.log: You bow. The straw rope sways without wind.

choices.text: Tell her the Landing never repaid anyone for any grief

effects.log: She stops. "No," she says. "It never did." It is not a concession.

events.text: It takes {crt_kin}, {crt_rel} of {crt_name}, some ages to become what {crt_khe} needed to be. {crt_kHe} has done it. {crt_kHe} waits at the ferry landing when you come down with your bell, and you can see from the way the light moves on the water that {crt_khe} came alone.

choices.text: Meet {crt_khim} at the landing

ok.log: You win, and it is not a victory. {crt_kin} drops to one knee, breathing hard. You walk away with a bruise you will keep.

fail.log: The landing tilts and you go into the cold water. When you surface {crt_kin} is gone, and your bell with {crt_khim}.

choices.text: Put your bell down in the water, and tell {crt_khim} it is over

effects.log: The bell sinks. {crt_kin} watches the ripples, and neither of you moves for a long time.

choices.text: Slip away across the water by night

effects.log: You slip off on a night ferry. The landing stays in your mind.

events.text: You tie it where their road crosses yours: a cord of five colours with the wonhon wound in it, knotted three times. {crt_name} stops with a cup halfway to {crt_his} lips. {crt_He} does not know what has happened. {crt_He} only knows that the nectar has gone cold in the hand, and that something in the room is listening.

choices.text: Send {crt_him} a note, so that {crt_he} knows

effects.log: A single line in black ink. By nightfall the whole heavens know that {crt_name} has been marked.

choices.text: Tell nobody, and wait

effects.log: The waiting is the real rite. It lasts a month.

events.text: The oath asks for a loop round your own wrist too, and you tie it, and the wonhon settles into the weave like a moth into wool. Whatever befalls the knot befalls you. In some far hall {crt_name} spills a cup and cannot say why. You study the cord on your wrist, and the cord seems to study you.

choices.text: Keep your hands very still

effects.log: You keep them still for an hour. The cord goes quiet, as a sleeper might.

choices.text: Test the knot with one gentle pull

effects.log: A far bowl rattles. You regret the test.

events.text: A limit is the cruellest kind of writ: it caps what a god can become. You tie it to {crt_name} and feel the ceiling lower, one rung at a time. From now on {crt_he} will climb only so far, and not know why.

choices.text: Pull the knot tight

effects.log: Tight. You feel a small, cold satisfaction, and hate it.

choices.text: Loosen it by a hair

effects.log: A hair is not much. It is still something.

events.text: On the third knot the cord goes slack in your fingers. Far away {crt_name} starts awake with a cold ring around one wrist and a taste of river water, rises at once, and turns to face exactly where you are. The ring fades within the hour. What does not fade is that an enemy now knows to be one.

choices.text: Soothe the cord and burn it

effects.log: The cord burns black. The writ sulks for a week.

choices.text: Keep the cord for another time

effects.log: You coil it away. It is not finished with you.

events.text: {crt_name} tried. {crt_He} was always going to, and you have often wondered what it would look like. It looks like someone in the middle of a hall, in the middle of a sentence, who sits down very suddenly. The knot tightens round your own chest as well. Somewhere in the heavens a bowl is dropped.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let the knot rest

effects.log: It rests. You breathe shallowly, and it rests a little longer.

choices.text: Untie it, before anyone else has to see this

effects.log: You untie it with shaking hands. It comes loose like wet silk.

choices.text: Draw it closed

effects.log: You draw it. The cord goes still. So do you, for a while.

events.text: The limit bit back. {crt_name} reached for the next rung and the ceiling pushed; both of you felt it. A rattle in the temple, a stumble on the steps. Somewhere, an attendant says the master has turned the colour of old paper. You press a hand to your own chest, and the pressure matches.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let the knot rest

effects.log: Rest. You sit very still and wait for the knot to calm.

choices.text: Untie it, before anyone else has to see this

effects.log: The knot loosens. The weight lifts from both of you.

choices.text: Draw it closed

effects.log: The limit hardens. You feel it set, and wish you had not.

events.text: Somebody has told {crt_name} how it is done. Perhaps Ferry-priestess Dalrae; perhaps an old tablet; perhaps only a hot needle, a cup of strong spirit and a great deal of wanting to. The knot is cut. You know because you are on the floor, and your hands are open, and the cord lies in two black pieces on the altar-step.

choices.text: Get up. There is a great deal to do now

effects.log: You get up. The sanctum spins and settles. The work ahead is long.

choices.text: Lie there a little longer

effects.log: The stone is cool. You think about what the knot meant, and what it cost.

events.text: {crt_name} reached the next rung this season. You knew before anyone. It lasted about as long as a breath out, and then the knot took it back, the whole gain, between one heartbeat and the next. The temple is baffled. You are not, and you sit very still, hating how well it works.

choices.text: Let {crt_him} try again

effects.log: The next attempt comes in spring. The knot is waiting.

choices.text: Send {crt_him} a good healer, at your own cost

effects.log: Your favour pays for the healer. {crt_name} never learns who sent the visit.

events.text: {crt_name} has sent a gift for the festival of the year. {crt_He} sends one every year, and always on time. This year it is a jar of plum nectar and a message, in a beautiful hand, hoping that you are in good health. You turn the message over and over. It is the most dangerous thing in the temple.

choices.text: Drink the nectar

effects.log: It is wonderful nectar. You rest soundly, which is its own kind of insult.

choices.text: Pour it out on the ground, to be safe

effects.log: The ground drinks it without complaint. You feel foolish and relieved.

events.text: It takes as long to untie as it took to tie, and then the same again, because your hands have got to know what they are doing and to mean it. At dawn the cord comes apart, and it is only cord. {crt_name} wakes somewhere in the heavens and does not know why {crt_he} is smiling. The temple doves land in your court for the first time in an age.

choices.text: Burn the cord

effects.log: Grey smoke, one thin line, going straight up.

choices.text: Keep the cord, to remember

effects.log: It sits in a chest, harmless as old thread.

events.text: {crt_name} went down to the morning offering this spring and asked the god across the altar, with great courtesy, who they were. Thirty ages, those two. {crt_He} says it is a very kind face. {crt_He} knows every other face in the heavens, and not this one. The healers call it a fashionable forgetting. You know the name for it.

choices.text: Go and hear it for yourself

effects.log: You go. It is exactly as described, and worse in the details.

choices.text: Do not go. You know how it goes

effects.log: You stay home. The clouds go by. You have never seen so many.

events.text: {crt_kin} has reached your sanctum, footsore, the label still stitched to {crt_khis} mantle. {crt_kHe} accuses nobody. {crt_kHe} has heard you know old writs, and sets out what the line can pay for the cure. It is a good deal. It is also exactly what you would have asked.

choices.text: Tell {crt_khim} the cure, and call it back

effects.log: You tell it all, and mean it. {crt_kin} writes it down in a shaking hand.

choices.text: Name a price for what you know

effects.log: A price is named. {crt_kin} pays it without a word, and leaves without one.

choices.text: Say you know of no such cure

effects.log: You say it flatly. {crt_kin} looks at you for a moment and nods.

events.text: A younger kin of {crt_name} comes to the ferry landing and asks every boatman about a priest who knows old writs. The boatmen shake their heads and look at their oars. {crt_kin} gets as far as your gate by evening, and knocks, and says very quietly, "Please."

choices.text: Tell {crt_khim} the cure, and call it back

effects.log: You tell it, plainly. The knocking stops, and the quiet afterwards is kind.

choices.text: Name a price for what you know

effects.log: You name it. {crt_kin} pays it without a word.

choices.text: Say you know of no such cure

effects.log: The gate stays shut. Footsteps go away down the stair.

events.text: {crt_kin} is back, and no longer polite. {crt_kHe} has been to the Quiet Temple and to Ferry-priestess Dalrae, and lays on your altar a sheet with four names, three crossed out. "She says it would have to be you," {crt_khe} says. {crt_kHe} has a spear at {crt_khis} side, and has not touched it yet.

choices.text: Give {crt_khim} the cure, and be done

effects.log: You tell it. The spear stays lowered, and the relief is a physical thing.

choices.text: Sell it, at a price that hurts

effects.log: You name a price that makes {crt_kin} flinch. {crt_kHe} pays.

choices.text: Look at the spear, and say nothing

effects.log: The silence stretches. {crt_kin} does not raise it.

events.text: First frost. {crt_kin} stands on the pier below the sanctum, the label gone grey with weather, a spear in both hands. {crt_kHe} has come to take the cure out of you, whichever way it can be taken. {crt_kHe} looks very tired and very certain.

choices.text: Go down the pier to meet {crt_khim}

ok.log: You knock the spear aside and hold {crt_khim} still until the fight leaves {crt_khim}. It leaves slowly.

fail.log: The spear bites. {crt_kin} does not finish it. You are left on the pier, breathing, while a figure walks away.

choices.text: Walk down with empty hands, and give {crt_khim} the cure

effects.log: You hold out empty hands. The spear lowers. The relief on that face is terrible to see.

choices.text: Sell it to {crt_khim}, even now

effects.log: Even now. {crt_kin} pays, hollow-eyed. You do not look back.

events.text: It comes back to {crt_name} in the middle of a rite, they say, or it comes back in part. {crt_He} puts down {crt_his} cup and looks across the altar, and says a name. Nobody in the hall moves. The name is correct. Somewhere in the heavens a cord goes slack, and a long-held breath leaves a long-held temple.

choices.text: Stay away. This is theirs

effects.log: You stay away. It is the hardest thing you have done this age.

choices.text: Go and watch it from the pier

effects.log: You watch from a distance. Nobody sees you. It is bittersweet.

events.text: One spring {crt_name} walks out of the temple gate in good spirits and asks a boatman the way to {crt_his} own shrine. Nobody sees {crt_him} again, unless you count the stories: a courteous old deity on the quays, who knows everyone and is known by none. You count the stories. You count them often.

choices.text: Say the name of {crt_name} once, for the record

effects.log: One name, aloud, to nobody. The wind takes it.

choices.text: Forget about it. You are good at that

effects.log: You are. It is a little too easy.

events.text: You wake, and across the altar is a kind and tired face you have known for ages. You open your mouth to greet it, and you stop. In an offering-market, far away, a pleasant stranger writes something in a ledger, and the ink glows briefly grey. You have, you realise, lost a name of your own.

choices.text: Say nothing, and start writing things down

effects.log: You write everything. It is not enough. It is never enough.

choices.text: Greet it, anyway

effects.log: The face smiles. You do not know whose it is, and it does not seem to matter.

events.text: A bailiff in grey, Jin of the Book of Fates, sits down in the outer court of your temple and asks for a cup of water. The Bailiff drinks it. The Bailiff looks at your cord, counts its knots aloud, and then counts the places where a cord of that size ought to have been cut. "Priest of the writ," comes the quiet voice, "I have only one question."

choices.text: Say you are a humble priest, and offer more water

effects.log: You offer more water. The Bailiff drinks it, and says nothing, which is worse.

choices.text: Tell the Bailiff you have given it up. And do

effects.log: You say it, and then you mean it, between one breath and the next.

choices.text: Tell the Bailiff who it is being addressed

effects.log: The Bailiff nods slowly. The court goes quiet. You have crossed a line, and you know it.

events.text: Bailiff Jin stops you on the pilgrim road, in rain, at a place where neither shrine can see. It must have been planned for your benefit, you think, and not the Bailiff's. Two fingers untie the cord from your wrist, as one handles a dead mouse, and lay a seal of the Book on your palm. "Choose," says the Bailiff.

choices.text: Try to stop the Bailiff

ok.log: You stop the Bailiff, barely. A bow, a step back, and no ledger-staff drawn. Not today.

fail.log: The ledger-staff finds your ribs. You go to the ground and the Bailiff steps over you without a word.

choices.text: Hold out your cord, and renounce it all

effects.log: You hold it out. The Bailiff takes it, and for a moment looks almost sorry.

choices.text: Get away over the river

ok.log: You are across the river before the Bailiff has finished speaking. The rain hides everything.

fail.log: You slip on the wet bank and the river takes your sandals and your pride.

events.text: The Bailiff has grown old on your account. You had not thought of it until you see Jin at the foot of the temple stair, one hand on a staff, the ledger-staff on the back grey with handling. Jin has come alone, which is a courtesy and a threat. "It is only you and I, now," says the Bailiff. "Let us settle it."

choices.text: Come down, and finish it

ok.log: You come down. It is a long and weary fight, and in the end you stand where the Bailiff stood, and the temple goes quiet behind you.

fail.log: The Bailiff seals you, gently, with a hand that knows exactly where to press. The cord goes dead, and so do your arms.

choices.text: Come down, and hand over the rites

effects.log: You hand over the cords, the tablets, the little book. They are weighed, and accepted.

events.text: It is done, and done properly. Nothing you could point to: your hands work, and the cord is only a cord, and the dead still come to you with their griefs. But when you reach for the old cold, nothing answers. It is like reaching for a stair that has been taken away. You stand there a long moment with your hand out.

choices.text: Go on being a priest, since it seems you still are

effects.log: The dead still come. You listen to them with an unfamiliar, plain gentleness.

choices.text: Throw the cup into the river

effects.log: It falls and is swallowed. You do not hear it land.

events.text: You walk down to the landing with all of it: the cords, the tablets, the little book of hours and stairs. The Ferrywoman Ok-i is on the pier, mending nets, the lanterns already lit. She takes it from you, piece by piece, as one takes laundry from a child. When she has the last she sets it all on the fire and says, "Sit. Eat. You are very thin."

choices.text: Sit, and eat

effects.log: You eat river-bread and drink bitter tea. It is the best meal you have had in ages.

choices.text: Ask how long it takes

effects.log: "All your existence," she says. "I will teach you the first part."

events.text: Somebody says the name of {crt_name} in the divine exchange, and you turn your head before you can think. You can no longer hear it without a slight pull at the wrist, the way a kite tugs when there is no wind. The speaker moves on, never knowing. You stand there with your arm half-raised.

choices.text: Think about something else

effects.log: You do, with effort. The pull fades, slowly, like a bell dying.

choices.text: Let yourself think about it

effects.log: You let it in. It comes in warmly, and sits down.

events.text: As a godling you would not let anyone tie a thread around your wrist, not even for a feast. Now you pass a shrine with its five-coloured cords in the wind, and a coldness goes through you from an age you cannot remember. Your hand knows a knot your mind does not. A temple dove watches from the lintel.

choices.text: Leave an offering, for whoever it was

effects.log: A handful of grain on the sill. The dove takes a kernel, delicately.

choices.text: Remember how the knot goes

effects.log: Your fingers do the rest. When you look down there is a perfect knot in a scrap of thread.

events.text: Old Man Gal of the Barrows finds you at a field-edge fire that gives no warmth and rubs his knuckles over it anyway. "You keep your dead on a string like a farmer keeps geese," he says. "They are owed more than gratitude. The Barrow Fellowship knows what a grudge is for."

choices.text: Ask what it costs

effects.log: Old Man Gal grins with half his teeth and names nothing. The fire leans away from him.

choices.text: Say you will think about it

effects.log: "Think by all means," he says, and leaves a notched stick on the stile. "Come back when the thinking is done."

events.text: Beside a leaning boundary-stone Old Man Gal has you hold a red thread while he talks. A hedge curse, he says, is only a grudge with a road to walk on. Give the wonhon a name and a direction, and let the thread do the rest. Your hands shake on the thread, and the thread seems to find that quite natural.

choices.text: Practise on the thread until your hands stop shaking

effects.log: You practise through the afternoon, wind in the hawthorn. By dusk your hands are steady, and you wish they were not.

choices.text: Ask what became of the last learner

effects.log: "Went to market," says Gal, and examines his boots. You decide not to ask which market.

events.text: The second lesson is a knot tied between two names and drawn tight with a vow. Old Man Gal calls it the Knot-Oath: what binds a foe binds you. "Mind the weight," he says, setting a river stone on your palm. The stone is heavier than a stone has any right to be, and faintly warm.

choices.text: Tie it round the stone until it holds

effects.log: It holds on the ninth try. The oath settles in your chest like a second small heart.

choices.text: Ask what happens if the knot is cut

effects.log: He tells you, shortly. You would have liked a vaguer answer.

events.text: The third lesson is taught in an empty barn at midnight, where only owls can hear: how to take a name out of a village, out of the parish book, out of every mouth that ever spoke it, until even the dogs forget. Old Man Gal says it once, low, and watches your face rather than the rafters.

choices.text: Repeat it back, word for word

effects.log: Word for word. Something small and dear leaves the world as you do, and neither of you says what.

choices.text: Say you need time before you use it

effects.log: He nods. "All do. Few take it."

events.text: A tinker's boy brings a strip of burial-cloth with a rival's name inked on it and the sign of the Fellowship. The Fellowship does not say why. It rarely does. It pays in grave-cold qi, and it has a long memory for anyone who declines.

choices.text: Send a wonhon after the name

effects.log: The cloth burns in the lamp without smoke. The Fellowship will be pleased.

choices.text: Send the cloth back unread

effects.log: You return it with a civil word. The boy shivers at the chill on your fingers.

events.text: A crock arrives with no sender, sealed in burial-cloth, cold as a well in March. That is the Fellowship's payment, and the Fellowship's way of saying the business is done. Nobody thanks you. The farm dog will not cross the threshold for a week.

choices.text: Drink what is in it

effects.log: It is the clearest water you have ever tasted, and your qi runs colder for a while.

choices.text: Pour it over the thread instead
