effects.log: The thread drinks greedily. You do not like how glad it looks.

events.text: You pick a crossroads with a gallows-oak, as you were taught, and bind the name on with a hair of your own. The wonhon that comes off the thread was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}. It has never heard of {crt_name}. You tell it, twice, and it listens, and goes.

choices.text: Walk away without looking back

effects.log: You walk the long lane home. The hedgerows seem to lean in a little closer than before.

choices.text: Say the name a third time, so it cannot lose its way

effects.log: Three times, and the oak creaks as if a weight has settled on its branch.

events.text: A hedge curse goes out from your barn roof at moonrise. The wonhon you give the name to was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}, and it slips toward {crt_name} like a draught finding a gap. You feel the thread go slack, and a small bright hunger go with it.

choices.text: Count the church bells until it is out of hearing

effects.log: Seven bells. The thread hangs empty. You tell yourself it is only thread.

choices.text: Follow it in thought as far as you can

effects.log: You see a farmhouse, a table, a hand on a cup. Then the thread snaps.

events.text: You send the grudge at an elder of another house, a harder knot than a rival's. The wonhon from the thread was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}; you give it {crt_name} and a heading, and it goes with a sound like a kettle forgetting its fire.

choices.text: Seal the knot and wash your hands

effects.log: The water runs grey for a moment, then clears.

choices.text: Mark the day in your private tally

effects.log: Dates are a way of owning what you have done. You write it small.

events.text: Someone of high standing, a lord's steward or a head of a great house, is the name on the thread. The wonhon you send was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}. It hesitates at the weight of {crt_name}, and then it goes, because the knot is tied well and the Fellowship taught you to tie it.

choices.text: Breathe out, slowly

effects.log: It leaves you lighter and somehow lonelier. You do not mention either.

choices.text: Tell yourself it was only a test of the rite

effects.log: The thread does not believe you, but the thread has no one to tell.

events.text: It is not done at a crossroads but at the christening-stone where the parish brings its babies. You say {crt_name} to the wonhon, and then the names of {crt_his} kin, every one you can recall, and one by one the candles along the wall gutter out. By dawn the stone remembers nobody.

choices.text: Scrub the stone clean afterwards

effects.log: You scrub until your knuckles split. The stone stays blank in the one place you meant to leave marked.

choices.text: Leave it as it is, and go

effects.log: The stone stays blank. You do not look back, and your boots sound louder than they should.

events.text: Your news of {crt_name} comes secondhand, as it should: {crt_His} well has turned bitter, and {crt_his} horse will not cross the yard. {crt_He} has dreamed three nights of a figure at the bedpost with a red thread. No one in the district has yet connected it with you.

choices.text: Send a little more of yourself after it

effects.log: A second thread, finer than the first. The omen thickens by morning.

choices.text: Take a cup at the same alehouse and watch

effects.log: You watch {crt_him} pass, hollow-eyed. The ale is fine and you finish none of it.

events.text: The elder's farmhouse has begun to complain: tiles crack in the night, the milk sours, the hands ask to be moved. {crt_name} blames old age. A rumour says a hedge-doctor from the next valley has been hired to sweep the rafters. It will not be enough.

choices.text: Let the curse find its own pace

effects.log: It finds one. The news arrives in thin, steady drips.

choices.text: Walk past the farmhouse and look up

effects.log: The roof-tree sags in a way no wind explains. You walk on faster than you meant to.

events.text: Even great houses show omens. {crt_name} is seen to start at nothing, to refuse a dish, to leave a wedding early with a pale face. The household whispers. You hear it from a carter who has no idea what he is telling, and is paid well to forget.

choices.text: Pay for more news

effects.log: The carter delivers a little more, and a little more. It is a kind of company.

choices.text: Stop listening

effects.log: You stop, with effort. The silence is louder than the carter was.

events.text: {crt_name} has lost a whole rung between one harvest and the next, the way a house loses its heat. The neighbours have stopped calling. {crt_His} {crt_rel}, {crt_kin}, goes from physician to physician across three counties. A word from the Fellowship asks if you wish to press on, and encloses a pinch of grave-dust to help.

choices.text: Say you cannot help, and hand it back

effects.log: The packet goes back unopened. Something in you unclenches, and something else sulks.

choices.text: Keep the dust, for the thread to read

effects.log: The thread drinks it down. {crt_name} will lose another rung before the leaves turn.

events.text: An elder has taken to resting in the afternoon, then in the morning, then not rising. The household tells visitors it is a fashionable lassitude. {crt_name} sent away the last physician. The thread on your windowsill is humming, quietly, like a pot that has not yet boiled.

choices.text: Let it hum

effects.log: It hums for weeks. You grow used to the sound, which is the worst of it.

choices.text: Feed it a little grave-dust

effects.log: The humming deepens. It sounds like agreement.

events.text: A great house weakens in plain view. {crt_name} misses a gathering, then two. The county sends a physician who goes pale at the door and leaves without a fee. It is possible that nobody connects this to a thread on a quiet sill. It is also possible that somebody does.

choices.text: Watch the gathering lists

effects.log: Absences, written in neat ink. Each one is a small coin dropped into your account.

choices.text: Look away

effects.log: You look at your dog instead. It looks back.

events.text: {crt_name} has climbed to the Ridge Hermitage, and Abbot Dohyun has looked at the shadow {crt_he} casts, and sent every other monk out. For forty-nine days the hermitage has chanted without rest. You feel the thread tighten, then slacken, like a line when something large turns away.

choices.text: Pour grave-qi after it, and pull

effects.log: You pull until your arms shake. The chanting falters once, and recovers.

choices.text: Hold still, and let it hold or not

effects.log: You hold. The chant rises and falls. You learn what patience costs.

choices.text: Call it back while you still can

effects.log: The thread comes in, hand over hand, wet and grey. The chanting stops at once.

events.text: Mudang Haneul of the well-town has been sent for. She comes to {crt_name}'s farmhouse at dusk with her bell wrapped in cloth and sits on the step with her back to the door, as one sits with a frightened animal. The thread on your sill spasms. Something cold on the other end is being coaxed, patiently, to let go.

choices.text: Pour grave-qi after it, and pull

effects.log: The thread fights back harder than you expected. Somewhere, a bell is unwrapped.

choices.text: Hold still, and let it hold or not

effects.log: You hold. The bell sweeps. You feel the tide turn, slowly, against you.

choices.text: Call it back while you still can

effects.log: The thread comes home like a tired dog. A bell is set down, far away.

events.text: Exorcist Ma Yeongdo of the Temple of the Peach-Wood Sword has been told, in the way these things are told, that something is eating at {crt_name}. The Exorcist arrives with a peach-wood blade and two novices who know better than to ask. The thread trembles in your hand. A temple bell is ringing, three villages off, and each stroke hurts.

choices.text: Pour grave-qi after it, and pull

effects.log: The bell falters and recovers. You feel the blade-charm flare on the far end.

choices.text: Hold still, and let it hold or not

effects.log: You hold. The bell rings. You count the strokes and lose count.

choices.text: Call it back while you still can

effects.log: The thread comes in with a snap. Far away, the bell stops mid-stroke.

events.text: {crt_name} fights it alone, by sheer stubbornness, standing barefoot on the barn roof in the storm with {crt_his} arms spread wide. The thread on your sill bucks. Whatever else {crt_he} may be, this is not a rival who gives up. The wonhon wails, and the wail comes down the thread into your palm.

choices.text: Pour grave-qi after it, and pull

effects.log: You pull. The wail breaks, then rises, then breaks again.

choices.text: Hold still, and let it hold or not

effects.log: You hold. Storm, wail, thread. None of the three gives way.

choices.text: Call it back while you still can

effects.log: The wail goes up one last time and stops. The thread is quiet and wet in your palm.

events.text: It holds. Word reaches you by way of a weary physician: {crt_name} has been sent home with kindly words and a recipe for barley broth. Everything that could be done has been done. The thread hangs quiet, and your cottage feels like a barn after the harvest dance.

choices.text: Coil it up and go to bed

effects.log: You coil it. It is lighter than it was, and you sleep badly.

choices.text: Leave an offering at the crossroads

effects.log: A few coins and a heel of bread at the gallows-oak. The crows watch.

events.text: {crt_kin}, {crt_rel} of {crt_name}, has found out who you are. It took {crt_khim} four years and most of what the house had left. {crt_kHe} does not come with a blade. {crt_kHe} comes on foot to your door, with a small box of coin, and kneels on the flagstones. "Call it back," {crt_khe} says. "That is all I came to say."

choices.text: Take the coin, and call it back

effects.log: The coin is counted twice and the thread comes in. Nobody in the district will speak of this.

choices.text: Call it back, and leave the box where it is

effects.log: You call it back. The box stays by the door until the kneeler stops looking at it.

choices.text: Shut the door

effects.log: The latch clicks. Beyond the planks, someone is very still for a very long time.

events.text: {crt_name} has not left bed since the first hard frost. Three people still visit. {crt_He} no longer asks what is wrong. The other evening, they say, {crt_he} asked after you, of all people, and smiled in a way that frightened the nurse. The thread on your sill is very quiet.

choices.text: Let it finish

effects.log: You let it. The thread thins, then is gone.

choices.text: Stop here, and leave {crt_him} alive with what is left

effects.log: You stop. It is a half-mercy, and you know it.

choices.text: Offer it: swear the oath, and live

effects.log: You swear on the river stone. The knot closes round both of you.

choices.text: Call it back, even now

effects.log: You call it back. It comes slowly, as if it too was tired.

events.text: An elder, once feared, is dying slowly in a farmhouse where no one raises a voice. {crt_name} has stopped receiving letters. The physicians have quit. At the foot of the bed a red thread that only you can see is drawn tight as a bowstring. One more pull, or one release.

choices.text: Let it finish

effects.log: You let it. The farmhouse goes quiet, and stays so.

choices.text: Stop here, and leave {crt_him} alive with what is left

effects.log: You ease the thread. The elder lives, a husk of reputation.

choices.text: Offer it: swear the oath, and live

effects.log: The knot closes round both of you.

choices.text: Call it back, even now

effects.log: It comes, like a tide going out. The elder sleeps, at last.

events.text: A great house lies on the edge. The county has quietly drafted a successor. {crt_name} knows, in the way the dying know, that the thread is tied to a person and not an accident. The next dawn will decide it, and only your hand is on the line.

choices.text: Let it finish

effects.log: It finishes. The county announces the succession at noon.

choices.text: Stop here, and leave {crt_him} alive with what is left

effects.log: You stop. The seat will pass to another, and {crt_name} will live to watch.

choices.text: Offer it: swear the oath, and live

effects.log: The oath closes. You feel a great weight take its seat on your shoulders.

choices.text: Call it back, even now

effects.log: The thread goes slack. {crt_name} wakes at dawn and asks for tea.

events.text: They bury {crt_name} on a clear morning in the churchyard. You attend; a hedge-doctor has every reason to. Nobody at the graveside knows yet. You perform the rites, since nobody asked another, and you are very good. {crt_kin} thanks you with red eyes. A servant presses a small purse into your hand.

choices.text: Take the fee

effects.log: The purse is light and heavy at once. You do not count it.

choices.text: Stay behind, and tidy the grave

effects.log: You pull the weeds until dusk. Nobody sees you do it, which is the point.

events.text: You stop it there. {crt_name} wakes one morning with the cold gone from the room, and lies a long time before daring to breathe in. {crt_He} is alive, with a third of what {crt_he} had. The district goes on whispering about a mysterious decline. You do not correct the district.

choices.text: Send a small gift, with no name on it

effects.log: A basket of oat cakes, sent through a stranger. {crt_name} eats them, and does not ask.

choices.text: Put it out of your mind

effects.log: You manage it for a month. Then the month ends.

events.text: The elder survives, thin and silent, and gives up the headship a year later with a dignified little speech nobody quite believes. {crt_kin} will inherit. You watch from a distance as the house is slowly reorganised around a person who no longer leaves the parlour.

choices.text: Send a sealed note of respect

effects.log: No signature. The elder reads it twice and burns it.

choices.text: Leave it alone

effects.log: You do, and mostly succeed.

events.text: The house survives, but not the person: {crt_name} resigns the stewardship on grounds of health and retires to a cottage with a single servant. A lesser cousin takes the chair. The county records do not mention you. The thread on your sill has gone grey with disuse.

choices.text: Send a carter with grain

effects.log: The carter returns with an empty sack and a bow. Nothing else.

choices.text: Look at the thread and say nothing

effects.log: It lies there like a sleeping snake.

events.text: You call it back, hand over hand, for a night and a day. It does not want to come. It was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}, and you gave it somewhere to go, and now you are telling it to stop. It comes because you ask, and because the thread is stronger than its grief. It leaves a cold stain across your palm.

choices.text: Burn incense for the wonhon

effects.log: Grey smoke rises through the rafters. You say its old name once.

choices.text: Keep it from Old Man Gal

effects.log: A small lie, told to a person who tells larger ones. It sits easier than expected.

events.text: The wonhon returns early. You feel it come along the lane, puzzled, like a dog sent to fetch someone from an emptied house. {crt_name} is out of its reach now, and not by any art of yours. The thread trembles for a moment and then lies still.

choices.text: Take it back on the thread

effects.log: It comes easily, relieved to be called by a familiar voice.

choices.text: Laugh, since there is nobody else to

effects.log: You laugh. The rooks startle and rise, then settle.

events.text: It comes back at the third watch. You know it at once and have just time to set down your cup. Someone has cut it, with a psalm or a song or simply by being tired of fear, and now everything it was holds against you, cold, through the thread. The Shrine of the Old Bells is two hills away and you can hear it ringing.

choices.text: Go to Grandmother Sunbok for the cleansing

effects.log: She makes you wait three days at the stile, then cleanses you with salt and silence.

choices.text: Fight it off by your own name

effects.log: You say your name and your parentage, loudly, to the empty room. It hurts, and it works, mostly.

choices.text: Listen to what it has to say

effects.log: It speaks for an hour in a voice you almost know. You come away changed.

events.text: A great grudge rebounds like a cart overturned in a ford. It was {crt_who}, {crt_wrong}, and it comes home to you with every wrong it ever carried, faster than you can lift the thread. The rooks scatter. The lamps in the lane are lit, one by one, as if someone is walking past them.

choices.text: Go to Grandmother Sunbok for the cleansing

effects.log: She takes the stain with her bare hands. It will take months to fade.

choices.text: Fight it off by your own name

effects.log: You stand your ground. It costs you a good deal.

choices.text: Listen to what it has to say

effects.log: It is much louder than you expected and has much to say.

events.text: Mudang Haneul comes herself. She walks up the lane alone, with her bell wrapped in cloth, and sits on your step. You knew she would. "That one cried, you know," she says, "when I let it go. {crt_who}. It asked me why nobody had thought to ask it first." She does not say whether she means the wonhon or you.

choices.text: Ask her how you look

effects.log: "Tired," she says. "Like all of us who talk to the dead for a living." It is the kindest thing anyone has said all year.

choices.text: Tell her to go home

effects.log: She goes, unhurried. The step stays warm where she sat.

events.text: Grandmother Sunbok knows. Nobody told her. A strip of straw rope hangs across the door of the back room now, and she gives your lesson on the porch in the same voice as ever. As you leave she says, without turning: "Whatever you owe the dead, child, do not pay it in other people's years."

choices.text: Bow, and say nothing

effects.log: You bow. The straw rope sways without wind.

choices.text: Tell her the Shrine never repaid anyone for any grief

effects.log: She stops. "No," she says. "It never did." It is not a concession.

events.text: It takes {crt_kin}, {crt_rel} of {crt_name}, some years to become what {crt_khe} needed to be. {crt_kHe} has done it. {crt_kHe} waits at the ford when you come down with your bell, and you can see from the way the light moves on the water that {crt_khe} came alone.

choices.text: Meet {crt_khim} at the ford

ok.log: You win, and it is not a victory. {crt_kin} drops to one knee, breathing hard. You walk away with a bruise you will keep.

fail.log: The ford tilts and you go into the cold water. When you surface {crt_kin} is gone, and your bell with {crt_khim}.

choices.text: Put your bell down in the water, and tell {crt_khim} it is over

effects.log: The bell sinks. {crt_kin} watches the ripples, and neither of you moves for a long time.

choices.text: Slip away across the water by night

effects.log: You slip off over the stepping-stones. The ford stays in your mind.

events.text: At the stile where their lane meets yours you hang a five-coloured cord with the wonhon wound through it, and pull three knots. {crt_name} halts with a spoon half raised. {crt_He} cannot say what has happened. {crt_He} knows only that the broth has chilled in the bowl, and that the kitchen has gone attentive.

choices.text: Send {crt_him} a note, so that {crt_he} knows

effects.log: A single line in grey ink. By nightfall the whole district knows that {crt_name} has been marked.

choices.text: Tell nobody, and wait

effects.log: The waiting is the real rite. It lasts a month.

events.text: Because the oath demands it, you wind a turn of the cord about your own wrist, and feel the wonhon sink into the strands. Whatever the knot suffers, you suffer. Miles off {crt_name} drops a ladle and stares at it. You hold your wrist up to the lamp, and the cord stares back.

choices.text: Keep your hands very still

effects.log: You keep them still for an hour. The cord goes quiet, as a sleeper might.

choices.text: Test the knot with one gentle pull

effects.log: A far bowl rattles. You regret the test.

events.text: A limit is the cruellest kind of hedge curse: it caps what a person can become. You tie it to {crt_name} and feel the ceiling lower, one rung at a time. From now on {crt_he} will climb only so far, and not know why.

choices.text: Pull the knot tight

effects.log: Tight. You feel a small, cold satisfaction, and hate it.

choices.text: Loosen it by a hair

effects.log: A hair is not much. It is still something.

events.text: The third knot will not take; the cord slithers loose. {crt_name} wakes with a mark round one wrist and river-cold in the mouth, is out of bed in a breath, and looks straight toward your door. The mark smoulders grey for an hour and fades. The harm is done all the same: you are now a known enemy to someone who knows it.

choices.text: Soothe the thread and burn the cord

effects.log: The cord burns grey. The thread sulks for a week.

choices.text: Keep the cord for another time

effects.log: You coil it away. It is not finished with you.

events.text: {crt_name} tried. {crt_He} was always going to, and you have often wondered what it would look like. It looks like someone in the middle of a kitchen, in the middle of a sentence, who sits down very suddenly. The knot tightens round your own chest as well. Somewhere in the district a bowl is dropped.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let the knot rest

effects.log: It rests. You breathe shallowly, and it rests a little longer.

choices.text: Untie it, before anyone else has to see this

effects.log: You untie it with shaking hands. It comes loose like wet silk.

choices.text: Draw it closed

effects.log: You draw it. The cord goes still. So do you, for a while.

events.text: The limit snapped back. {crt_name} stretched for the next rung and met the ceiling, and you felt the jolt as if it were your own. Crockery rattled somewhere; a servant swears the master went the shade of tallow. Your palm presses your breastbone, and the ache beneath it keeps time.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let the knot rest

effects.log: Rest. You sit very still and wait for the knot to calm.

choices.text: Untie it, before anyone else has to see this

effects.log: The knot loosens. The weight lifts from both of you.

choices.text: Draw it closed

effects.log: The limit hardens. You feel it set, and wish you had not.

events.text: Somebody has told {crt_name} how it is done. Perhaps Mudang Haneul; perhaps an old almanac; perhaps only a hot needle, a cup of strong spirit and a great deal of wanting to. The knot is cut. You know because you are on the floor, and your hands are open, and the cord lies in two grey pieces on the sill.

choices.text: Get up. There is a great deal to do now

effects.log: You get up. The room spins and settles. The work ahead is long.

choices.text: Lie there a little longer

effects.log: The boards are cool. You think about what the knot meant, and what it cost.

events.text: Word comes that {crt_name} won the next rung over the winter. It held for a single breath, and then the knot reclaimed the lot between two heartbeats. The household is bewildered. You are not, and you sit absolutely still, disliking how well your work performs.

choices.text: Let {crt_him} try again

effects.log: The next attempt comes in spring. The knot is waiting.

choices.text: Send {crt_him} a good physician, at your own cost

effects.log: You pay him ten taels. {crt_name} never learns who sent the visit.

events.text: A parcel from {crt_name} turns up at midwinter, as it does every year, never late: a stoneware jar of plum wine and a letter in lovely handwriting wishing you health. You turn the letter over and over. Nothing in the cottage has ever felt so risky.

choices.text: Keep the wine for a guest

effects.log: Your guests say it is wonderful wine. You sleep soundly anyway, which is its own kind of insult.

choices.text: Pour it out on the ground, to be safe

effects.log: The ground drinks it without complaint. You feel foolish and relieved.

events.text: It takes as long to untie as it took to tie, and then the same again, because your hands have got to know what they are doing and to mean it. At dawn the cord comes apart, and it is only cord. {crt_name} wakes somewhere in the district and does not know why {crt_he} is smiling. The rooks land in your yard for the first time in a year.

choices.text: Burn the cord

effects.log: Grey smoke, one thin line, going straight up.

choices.text: Keep the cord, to remember

effects.log: It sits in a drawer, harmless as old thread.

events.text: {crt_name} went down to breakfast this spring and asked the one across the table, with great courtesy, who they were. Thirty years, those two. {crt_He} says it is a very kind face. {crt_He} knows every other face in the district, and not this one. The physicians call it a fashionable forgetting. You know the name for it.

choices.text: Go and hear it for yourself

effects.log: You go. It is exactly as described, and worse in the details.

choices.text: Do not go. You know how it goes

effects.log: You stay home. The clouds go by. You have never seen so many.

events.text: {crt_kin} has reached your door, footsore, the label still sewn to {crt_khis} coat. {crt_kHe} accuses nobody. {crt_kHe} has heard you know old curses, and sets out what the house can pay for the cure. It is a good deal. It is also exactly what you would have asked.

choices.text: Tell {crt_khim} the cure, and call it back

effects.log: You tell it all, and mean it. {crt_kin} writes it down in a shaking hand.

choices.text: Name a price for what you know

effects.log: A price is named. {crt_kin} pays it without a word, and leaves without one.

choices.text: Say you know of no such cure

effects.log: You say it flatly. {crt_kin} looks at you for a moment and nods.

events.text: A younger kin of {crt_name} comes to the carrier's yard and asks every drover about a hedge-doctor who knows old curses. The drovers shake their heads and look at their whips. {crt_kin} gets as far as your gate by evening, and knocks, and says very quietly, "Please."

choices.text: Tell {crt_khim} the cure, and call it back

effects.log: You tell it, plainly. The knocking stops, and the quiet afterwards is kind.

choices.text: Name a price for what you know

effects.log: You name it. {crt_kin} pays it without a word.

choices.text: Say you know of no such cure

effects.log: The gate stays shut. Footsteps go away down the lane.

events.text: {crt_kin} is back, and no longer polite. {crt_kHe} has been to the Ridge Hermitage and to Mudang Haneul, and lays on your table a sheet with four names, three crossed out. "She says it would have to be you," {crt_khe} says. {crt_kHe} has a cudgel at {crt_khis} belt, and has not touched it yet.

choices.text: Give {crt_khim} the cure, and be done

effects.log: You tell it. The cudgel stays at the belt, and the relief is a physical thing.

choices.text: Sell it, at a price that hurts

effects.log: You name a price that makes {crt_kin} flinch. {crt_kHe} pays.

choices.text: Look at the cudgel, and say nothing

effects.log: The silence stretches. {crt_kin} does not draw it.

events.text: First frost. {crt_kin} stands in the lane below the cottage, the label gone grey with weather, a cudgel in both hands. {crt_kHe} has come to take the cure out of you, whichever way it can be taken. {crt_kHe} looks very tired and very certain.

choices.text: Go down the lane to meet {crt_khim}

ok.log: You turn the blow aside and hold {crt_khim} still until the fight leaves {crt_khim}. It leaves slowly.

fail.log: The cudgel lands. {crt_kin} does not finish it. You are left in the lane, breathing, while a figure walks away.

choices.text: Walk down with empty hands, and give {crt_khim} the cure

effects.log: You hold out empty hands. The cudgel lowers. The relief on that face is terrible to see.

choices.text: Sell it to {crt_khim}, even now

effects.log: Even now. {crt_kin} pays, hollow-eyed. You do not look back.

events.text: It comes back to {crt_name} in the middle of a meal, they say, or it comes back in part. {crt_He} puts down {crt_his} spoon and looks across the table, and says a name. Nobody at that table moves. The name is correct. Somewhere in the district a thread goes slack, and a long-held breath leaves a long-held house.

choices.text: Stay away. This is theirs

effects.log: You stay away. It is the hardest thing you have done this year.

choices.text: Go and watch it from the lane

effects.log: You watch from a distance. Nobody sees you. It is bittersweet.

events.text: One spring {crt_name} walks out of {crt_his} own gate in good spirits and asks a carter the way to {crt_his} own house. Nobody sees {crt_him} again, unless you count the stories: a courteous old person on the market road, who knows everyone and is known by none. You count the stories. You count them often.

choices.text: Say the name of {crt_name} once, for the record

effects.log: One name, aloud, to nobody. The wind takes it.

choices.text: Forget about it. You are good at that

effects.log: You are. It is a little too easy.

events.text: You wake, and across the table is a kind and tired face you have known for years. You open your mouth to say good morning, and you stop. In a salt store, far away, a pleasant man writes something in a ledger, and the ink glows briefly grey. You have, you realise, lost a name of your own.

choices.text: Say nothing, and start writing things down

effects.log: You write everything. It is not enough. It is never enough.

choices.text: Say good morning, anyway

effects.log: The face smiles. You do not know whose it is, and it does not seem to matter.

events.text: A man with a peach-wood sword sits down in the outer yard and asks for a cup of water. He drinks it. He looks at your thread, counts its knots aloud, and then counts the places where a thread of that size ought to have been cut. "Hedge-doctor," says Exorcist Ma Yeongdo, "I have only one question."

choices.text: Say you are a poor healer, and offer more water

effects.log: You offer more water. He drinks it, and says nothing, which is worse.

choices.text: Tell him you have given it up. And do

effects.log: You say it, and then you mean it, between one breath and the next.

choices.text: Tell him who it is he is talking to

effects.log: He nods slowly. The yard goes quiet. You have crossed a line, and you know it.

events.text: Ma Yeongdo stops you on the ferry road, in rain, at a place where neither bank can see. He must have planned that for your benefit, you think, and not for his. He unties the thread from your wrist with two fingers, as one handles a dead mouse, and lays a peach-wood charm on your palm. "Choose," he says.

choices.text: Try to stop him

ok.log: You stop him, barely. He steps back, bows, and does not draw the blade. Not today.

fail.log: The peach-wood blade finds your ribs. You go to the ground and he steps over you without a word.

choices.text: Hold out your thread, and renounce it all

effects.log: You hold it out. He takes it, and for a moment looks almost sorry.

choices.text: Get away over the river

ok.log: You are across the river before he has finished speaking. The rain hides everything.

fail.log: You slip on the wet bank and the river takes your boots and your pride.

events.text: He has grown old on your account. You had not thought of it until you see him at the foot of the lane, one hand on a stick, the peach-wood blade on his back grey with handling. He has come alone, which is a courtesy and a threat. "It is only you and I, now," Ma Yeongdo says. "Let us settle it."

choices.text: Come down, and finish it

ok.log: You come down. It is a long and weary fight, and in the end you stand where he stood, and the lane goes quiet behind you.

fail.log: He seals you, gently, with a hand that knows exactly where to press. The thread goes dead, and so do your arms.

choices.text: Come down, and hand him the rites

effects.log: You hand over the threads, the slips, the little book. He weighs them, and nods.

events.text: It is done, and done properly. Nothing you could point to: your hands work, and the thread is only a thread, and the dead still come to you with their griefs. But when you reach for the old cold, nothing answers. It is like reaching for a stair that has been taken away. You stand there a long moment with your hand out.

choices.text: Go on being a hedge-doctor, since it seems you still are

effects.log: The dead still come. You listen to them with an unfamiliar, plain gentleness.

choices.text: Throw the cup into the river

effects.log: It falls and is swallowed. You do not hear it land.

events.text: You walk up the hill with all of it: the threads, the slips, the little book of hours and stairways. Grandmother Sunbok is at the top, cutting straw, the fires already lit. She takes it from you, piece by piece, as one takes laundry from a child. When she has the last she sets it all on the fire and says, "Sit. Eat. You are very thin."

choices.text: Sit, and eat

effects.log: You eat barley bread and drink bitter tea. It is the best meal you have had in years.

choices.text: Ask how long it takes

effects.log: "All your life," she says. "I will teach you the first part."

events.text: Somebody says the name of {crt_name} in the market, and you turn your head before you can think. You can no longer hear it without a slight pull at the wrist, the way a kite tugs when there is no wind. The speaker moves on, never knowing. You stand there with your arm half-raised.

choices.text: Think about something else

effects.log: You do, with effort. The pull fades, slowly, like a bell dying.

choices.text: Let yourself think about it

effects.log: You let it in. It comes in warmly, and sits down.

events.text: As a child you would not let anyone tie a thread around your wrist, not even for a birthday. Now you pass a roadside shrine with its five-coloured cords in the wind, and a coldness goes through you from a life you cannot remember. Your hand knows a knot your mind does not. A sparrow watches from the lintel.

choices.text: Leave an offering, for whoever it was

effects.log: A handful of rice on the sill. The sparrow takes a grain, delicately.

choices.text: Remember how the knot goes

effects.log: Your fingers do the rest. When you look down there is a perfect knot in a scrap of thread.
